analysis.title: FX Daily: US inflation to offer some support to USD today
key_insights: The dollar has given back most of last week's gains as global equities rebounded and oil extended its decline. The Nasdaq and S&P 500 are less than 2% below their 4 November closing levels despite a 4% drop in Nvidia stock tied to an investigation into its CEO, which ING reads as a bout of jitters rather than the start of a bigger downturn.

ING expects October US core CPI at 0.3% MoM, slightly above consensus, and headline CPI at 0.3% MoM, in line with consensus. This should give front-end USD rates some support. YoY figures are not published this month because of last year's government shutdown.

A 0.3% MoM print is consistent with the Fed meeting its inflation target of 0.17%. Barring a downward surprise, ING says it will be hard for FOMC members to sound materially less hawkish on the back of the stock market troubles. Speakers today include Waller and Bowman (seen as most dovish) and Logan and Schmid (seen as most hawkish).

EUR/USD has returned to a 1.5-1.7% undervaluation on ING's models after rebounding yesterday. French risk argues against another fast narrowing of the valuation gap. ING expects the pair to stabilise in the 1.120-1.1250 area this week, with a moderate positive bias into year-end and a year-end target of 1.130.

Falling oil prices on renewed Middle East optimism may give EUR/USD limited support alone. Short-term rate differentials matter more. A further energy decline could cause a larger repricing in ECB rate expectations relative to the Fed's, especially if US CPI builds a stronger floor for front-end USD rates.

Norway's October headline CPI rose from 3.4% to 3.6%, below the 3.7% consensus. Underlying CPI-ATE slowed as expected from 3.0% to 2.7%. ING reads this as supporting a prolonged pause by Norges Bank at 4.50%, with cuts in 2027 earlier than most other central banks.
Markets price about a one-in-three chance of another Norges Bank hike by March and 10bp of easing over the next year. EUR/NOK has rebounded to within ING's 10.55-10.65 year-end target range.

Hungarian CPI rose from 1.6% to 2.0% in October, in line with expectations and the lowest in CEE. ING expects it to peak slightly below 4% in mid-2027, which would allow NBH rate cuts in the second half of next year. Hungary is significantly exposed to energy prices.
Final Czech October CPI is due today after a flash estimate of 2.4% (from 2.5%). ING expects core to rise from 3.1% to 3.2%. CNB's new forecast is due Friday.

CEE rates rallied again as the market priced out rate hikes after energy prices fell. FX gains were limited. Narrowing rate differentials and a strong USD are headwinds, and the rate rally points to a weaker outlook for regional FX once the current stabilisation ends.

tension_points.bull_case: EUR/USD is 1.5-1.7% undervalued and lower oil prices on Middle East optimism may offer some support.
tension_points.bear_case: Rate differentials matter more than oil. A stronger US CPI floor for front-end USD rates and a larger fall in ECB pricing relative to the Fed's would cap the rally, and French risk argues against fast tightening of the valuation gap.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A downward surprise in today's US CPI would remove the support for front-end USD rates that underpins ING's view of a stabilising EUR/USD.
